sections.technical: Visit CISA’s PQC Initiative page for additional resources.
sections.impact:
CISA, the Australian Signals Directorate’s Australian Cyber Security Centre (ASD’s ACSC) and the National Security Agency (NSA) released joint guidance and an accompanying quick-reference list to help organizations assess vendor readiness for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). As quantum computing advances, widely used public-key cryptography will become vulnerable to compromise from cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs). To protect their systems and data, organizations must plan for and transition to PQC—which includes algorithms capable of withstanding both classical computing and quantum-enabled threats—before CRQCs become available.

Assessed severity: LOW.
sections.mitigation: To protect their systems and data, organizations must plan for and transition to PQC—which includes algorithms capable of withstanding both classical computing and quantum-enabled threats—before CRQCs become available. Cryptography is also embedded in systems and devices that are difficult to update, tied to long asset lifecycles, and require vendor support or replacement—such as industrial control systems and Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

title: US Government Partners Urge Hardening Industrial Refrigeration and Cold Chain Monitoring Systems
summary: Overview
card_summary: Overview

sections.overview:
Overview 
 The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Health and Human Services (HHS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DoT)—hereafter referred to as “the authoring organizations”—are aware of malicious cyber activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems globally.
sections.impact:
Contact HHS via HHSCyber@hhs.gov or the HHS 24/7 Operations Center at 202-619-7800 for assistance mitigating potential disruptions to the delivery of healthcare resulting from health and medical supply chain impacts. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DoT)—hereafter referred to as “the authoring organizations”—are aware of malicious cyber activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems globally. Threat 
 The authoring organizations are aware of malicious cyber actors targeting electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.

Assessed severity: HIGH.
sections.mitigation:
Should remote access be necessary, protect it by using a firewall or edge device and updating it to the latest version to reduce security vulnerabilities. To strengthen system security, owners and operators should review the following resources and implement recommended mitigations:

 
 CISA: Primary Mitigations to Reduce Cyber Threats to Operational Technology 

 CISA: Defend the Edge: The Critical Importance of Edge Device Security 

 CISA: Internet Exposure Reduction Guidance 

 United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre and Partners: Secure Connectivity Principles for OT 

 
 Contact Information 
 The authoring organizations recommend U.S. organizations report suspicious or criminal activity related to information provided in this fact sheet:

 
 Contact CISA via CISA’s 24/7 Operations Center at contact@cisa.dhs.gov or 1-844-Say-CISA (1-844-729-2472). Mitigations 
 The authoring organizations urge owners and operators to immediately take the following actions. The CPGs provide a minimum set of practices and protections that CISA and NIST recommend all organizations implement:

 
 Eliminate public internet exposure : Do not expose control system devices and/or systems, particularly controller panels, to the internet [ CPG 3.S ].
